newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: "Please use a condom," says Archbishop Tutu.
newsitem.headline: "Please use a condom," says Archbishop Tutu.

text.p: Anglican Archbishop Desmond Tutu called on Sunday for South Africans to use condoms if they did not stick to Christian teachings on sex.

Tutu, a Nobel peace prizewinner and the head of the country's "truth commission" into apartheid-era atrocities, appeared in a television advertisement for state television as part of South Africa's campaign to mark World AIDS day.
"Our wonderful country faces a major crisis with HIV and AIDS spreading so fast," said a serious-looking Tutu, sitting in his study in a purple cassock with a gold cross around his neck.
"We in the church believe that sex should take place only within marriage.
"However, I want to urge all those who choose to have sex outside of marriage to take the right precautions and practise safer sex.

South Africa's health department said latest research showed that around 4.5 percent of the roughly 40 million people in the country were infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which can cause the killer disease.
Tutu appeared in the public service advertisement for the Society for Family Health, which is a non-profit, non-governmental organisation.
The society's condoms are on sale at a quarter of the price of commercial brands to draw lower income consumers.
